summary: Chapter-sized candidates are a defensible temporary coverage scaffold, but chapter edges are editorial coordinates rather than proof of speaker turns. Keep low confidence and do not promote the generic dialogue_speech_cycle labels as speaker or theology metadata.

high_risk_translation_holds.risk: vision report, ruach/nishmah vocabulary, and rhetorical questions permit materially different English segmentation
bene-resheph (‘sparks’/‘sons of flame’) and quotation-like wisdom formulas; 5:13 has a canonical cross-reference to 1Cor.3.19 but that does not establish a chunk boundary
hesed toward the despairing, taunt/abandonment terms, and tsaba (‘hard service/appointed time’) are translation-sensitive
mokhiach (‘arbiter/mediator’) and court vocabulary can be overread as doctrinal terminology
Zophar’s compressed rhetoric and ‘double’ language are ambiguous; do not normalize into a moral formula
wisdom hymn-like catalogue may be quotation, poetic assertion, or disputation; preserve alternatives
‘holy ones’ and purity language have multiple possible referents and should not be mapped to a fixed supernatural taxonomy
pronoun/agent ambiguity in ‘he tears’ and witness/advocate terminology; Hebrew discourse review required
‘firstborn of death’ and disease/terror imagery are idiomatic; avoid medical or demonological labels
go’el (‘redeemer/kinsman’) and 19:26 body/skin wording have major textual/translation variants; must remain an appeal item
poison/serpent and swallowed-riches imagery is figurative and lexically unstable
Eliphaz’s alleged charges use rare terms and are character claims, not verified biography
‘my way’ and darkness/terror clauses support several rhetorical readings; do not force a conversion or verdict narrative
social-injustice catalogue has disputed segmentation and rare vocabulary; preserve as one parent with internal case map
Sheol/Rahab/cosmic imagery and sarcasm are translation-sensitive; labels must stay descriptive
oath, enemy formula, and wicked-person fate resemble earlier friend speeches; speaker/compositional attribution is unresolved

red_team_findings.finding: The current per-chapter generic label hides known speaker sequence and could be misread as a chapter-authoritative speaker assignment.
red_team_findings.recommendation: Keep generic labels or add qualified sequence labels only in candidate sidecars; require external/human review before speaker metadata is promoted.

red_team_findings.finding: Job 27:13-23 is not safely treated as an uncontested Job continuation.
red_team_findings.recommendation: Retain parent Job.26.1-Job.27.23 and record alternatives (Job speech versus residual friend-speech/compositional seam) without selecting one.

red_team_findings.finding: Chapter boundaries at 5/7/10/14/17/19/21/24/27 do not necessarily coincide with speech closure; conversely internal seams can occur within chapters.
red_team_findings.recommendation: Use chapter spans for coverage only; add internal seam candidates and do not split solely by chapter.

red_team_findings.finding: Terms such as ‘mediator’, ‘redeemer’, ‘divine speech’, and ‘holy ones’ can smuggle theological conclusions.
red_team_findings.recommendation: Use neutral lexical descriptions (‘witness/court imagery’, ‘agent attribution held’, ‘poetic question sequence’) until original-language and cross-environment review.

red_team_findings.finding: Cross-references (e.g., Job 5:13/1 Cor 3:19; Job 19:25 and later biblical reuse) can improperly force boundaries or harmonize voices.
red_team_findings.recommendation: Record cross-reference pointers as evidence-only relations; never use them as automatic chunk or interpretation authority.

required_next_checks: controller-observed Hebrew/Aramaic lexical review with verse-numbering crosswalk
independent literary-form review distinguishing speech, hymn, lament, and catalogue without theological inference
cross-reference review that records relations but cannot move candidate boundaries by itself
speaker/composition appeal ledger for Job 27:13-23 and any disputed quotation-like units
external-provider and human review before any promotion
